mainTopic: The עיר מקלט: road signs and how הקדוש ברוך הוא guides people, the גואל הדם who kills the רוצח, who runs to an עיר מקלט, and cities that cannot take a killer in.
overview: The amud opens with the signs reading 'מקלט' that were posted at every crossroads, and רב כהנא gives the פסוק behind them. Two openings to the topic follow. רב חמא בר חנינא teaches that if הקדוש ברוך הוא guides sinners, He surely guides צדיקים. ריש לקיש explains how הקדוש ברוך הוא brings two unpunished killers together so each one gets what he deserves. Then the גמרא teaches that a person is led along whatever path he chooses, with proof from the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים. Back in the הלכה, רב הונא rules that a גואל הדם who kills the רוצח on his way to exile is פטור. The גמרא defends him against a ברייתא and against the משנה about the two תלמידי חכמים. A ברייתא then shows that at first even a מזיד runs to the עיר מקלט until בית דין judges him. Next, רבי אלעזר rules on cities that do not take in a killer: a city made up mostly of killers, and a city with no זקנים. רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue whether 'elders' are required in three cases: עיר מקלט, בן סורר ומורה and עגלה ערופה. The amud ends as רבי חמא בר חנינא begins asking why the פרשה of רוצחים was said; the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'Refuge' was posted at crossroads
steps.stepSummary: Signs reading 'מקלט' stood at every crossroads to guide the accidental killer to a city of refuge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'Refuge' was written at the crossroads, so the killer would recognize the way and turn there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a practical rule: at every fork in the road there was a sign reading 'מקלט' pointing toward the city of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רוצח בשוגג has to get to the עיר מקלט quickly, before the גואל הדם catches him. The signs make sure he never loses time choosing the wrong road.

keyTerms.meaning: Refuge; the city of refuge where an accidental killer is protected
Killer; here, one who killed by accident

phrases.english: "Refuge" was written
at the crossroads,
so that the killer would recognize the way

steps.triggerLanguage: מקלט היה כתוב על פרשת דרכים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Signs reading 'מקלט' were placed at every crossroads to direct the accidental killer.

steps.title: רב כהנא's verse for the road signs
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings the פסוק 'תכין לך הדרך' as the source for posting the signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: What is the verse? 'Prepare for you the road' means: make preparation for the road.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks where the sign rule comes from in the תורה and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'תכין לך הדרך' are read as an order to get the road ready for the person running there. Putting up direction signs is part of that preparation, so the sign rule has a source in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for the scriptural source)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: What is the verse?
"Prepare for you the road"
phrases.notes: דברים 19:3

phrases.english: make [for you] preparation for the road.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions leave it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי קרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the rule in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that signs were posted at crossroads
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 19:3, 'תכין לך הדרך', read as 'make preparation for the road'

steps.title: If God guides sinners, all the more so the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר חנינא opens the topic with תהלים: הקדוש ברוך הוא guides even sinners, so He surely guides צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר חנינא introduced this section from here: 'Good and upright is ה׳; therefore He guides sinners on the way.' If He guides sinners, all the more so the righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the road signs, רב חמא בר חנינא gives an opening thought for this whole section, using a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs show הקדוש ברוך הוא guiding even a person who killed through carelessness. From this he makes a קל וחומר: if a sinner is helped to find his way, a צדיק will surely be guided too.

keyTerms.meaning: Opened with an opening; introduced the topic with a verse from elsewhere
Section of the תורה (here, the section about the cities of refuge)
An 'all the more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Chanina

phrases.aramaic: פָּתַח לַהּ פִּתְחָא לְהַאי פָּרַשְׁתָּא מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: opened an opening for this section from here:
phrases.notes: This means he started his talk on this section with a verse from another part of תנ״ך.

phrases.english: "Good and upright is ה׳;
therefore He guides sinners on the way"
phrases.notes: תהלים 25:8

phrases.english: If He guides sinners,

steps.triggerLanguage: פתח לה פתחא להאי פרשתא מהכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson about God's kindness from the road-sign rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since הקדוש ברוך הוא guides sinners, by קל וחומר He guides צדיקים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש quotes two verses to open the section
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש quotes 'והאלהים אנה לידו' and 'מרשעים יצא רשע' as his opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש introduced this section from here: 'And one who did not lie in wait, but God caused it to come to his hand…' and 'As the ancient parable says: From the wicked comes forth wickedness…'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש quotes two פסוקים. This step sets things up; his explanation of how the פסוקים fit together comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says God 'caused' the accidental killing, which is puzzling: why would God bring about a death? The second פסוק hints at the answer: bad things come out of people who are already wicked.

keyTerms.meaning: Caused it to happen through him

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish

phrases.aramaic: פָּתַח לַהּ פִּתְחָא לְהַאי פָּרַשְׁתָּא מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: opened an opening for this section from here:
"And one who did not lie in wait,
phrases.notes: שמות 21:13

phrases.english: but God caused it to come to his hand, etc."
"As the ancient parable says:
phrases.notes: שמואל א 24:13

phrases.english: From the wicked comes forth wickedness, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון בן לקיש פתח לה פתחא להאי פרשתא מהכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different opening to the same section, parallel to רב חמא בר חנינא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The accidental killing that 'God caused' is linked to the idea that wickedness comes from the wicked.

steps.title: The case: two unpunished killers
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש describes two killers, one accidental and one intentional, with no witnesses to either killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the verse talking about? Two people who killed someone. One killed by accident and one killed on purpose. Neither had witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש begins explaining the פסוק by describing the situation it has in mind. He is setting up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no witnesses, בית דין cannot punish anyone. The שוגג was never sent to גלות, and the מזיד was never put to death, so both are 'wicked' people whose sins are still unpunished.

keyTerms.meaning: About what case is the verse speaking?

phrases.english: About what is the verse speaking?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁהָרְגוּ אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
phrases.english: About two people who killed a person,
one killed unintentionally
and one killed intentionally,

phrases.aramaic: לָזֶה אֵין עֵדִים וְלָזֶה אֵין עֵדִים.
phrases.english: this one has no witnesses and that one has no witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: במה הכתוב מדבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the פסוקים quoted in step 4 by describing the case they refer to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is about two killers, one שוגג and one מזיד, who both escaped punishment because there were no witnesses.

steps.title: God brings them together so each gets his due
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא brings both men to one inn. The accidental killer falls off a ladder onto the intentional killer and kills him, so the מזיד dies and the שוגג goes into גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: God brings them to one inn. The one who killed on purpose sits under a ladder. The one who killed by accident comes down the ladder, falls on him and kills him. So the intentional killer is killed, and the accidental killer goes into exile.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש finishes his explanation: God arranges a meeting so that both killers finally receive the punishment they deserved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains 'והאלהים אנה לידו': God 'caused' this accidental death because the victim deserved to die. It also fits 'מרשעים יצא רשע': the new killing came through someone who was already guilty, and this time it happens in public, so the שוגג is sent to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes into exile (to the city of refuge)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש teaches that even when בית דין cannot act, הקדוש ברוך הוא makes sure the guilty get exactly what they deserve: death for the מזיד and גלות for the שוגג.
steps.confusionAlert: The intentional killer is not executed by בית דין here. He 'is killed' by the accidental fall, and that death is his punishment.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the תורה says God 'caused' an accidental death: the victim was already guilty, and the killer also deserved גלות.

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְמִינָן לְפוּנְדָּק אֶחָד,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, brings them to one inn,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁהָרַג בְּמֵזִיד יוֹשֵׁב תַּחַת הַסּוּלָּם,
phrases.english: the one who killed intentionally sits beneath the ladder,
and the one who killed unintentionally is coming down the ladder,
and he falls on him and kills him.
The one who killed intentionally is killed,
and the one who killed unintentionally goes into exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: הקדוש ברוך הוא מזמינן לפונדק אחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story set up in step 5 and shows how it explains the פסוקים in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'והאלהים אנה לידו' means הקדוש ברוך הוא arranges for the unpunished intentional killer to die through the unpunished accidental killer, so each gets his deserved punishment.

steps.title: A person is led along the path he wants to take
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר (or רב הונא, in the other version) teaches that a person is led along whatever path he chooses. He says this is found in the תורה, the נביאים, and the כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב הונא, and some say רב הונא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: From the תורה, the נביאים, and the כתובים we learn that a person is led along the path he wants to go.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous steps showed how הקדוש ברוך הוא guides people. Now the גמרא brings a related statement: whichever way a person wants to go, he is helped to go that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new idea to the earlier steps. Those steps showed God steering events, as with the two killers at the inn. This statement says the person's own choice sets the direction, and he is then helped along it. The claim is that all three parts of תנ"ך teach this, and the next step brings those three sources.

keyTerms.meaning: They lead him, meaning he is helped along
The three parts of תנ"ך: the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings
On the path a person wants to walk

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav Huna said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna said that Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַתּוֹרָה וּמִן הַנְּבִיאִים וּמִן הַכְּתוּבִים –
phrases.english: From the Torah, from the Prophets, and from the Writings,
along the path a person wants to go,
they lead him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the earlier steps, that הקדוש ברוך הוא guides people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is led along the path he chooses to go.

steps.title: Three פסוקים prove the idea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings one פסוק each from the תורה (בלעם), the נביאים (ישעיהו), and the כתובים (משלי). Each shows that a person is led along the path he chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the Torah, as it says, 'Do not go with them,' and then it says, 'Get up, go with them.' From the Prophets, as it says, 'I am ה׳ your God, Who teaches you for your benefit, Who leads you on the path you go.' From the Writings, as it says, 'If it is for the scoffers, He makes him scoff, and to the humble He gives grace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the three sources promised in the previous step, one from each part of תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תורה, God first tells בלעם not to go, but once בלעם wants to go, God tells him to go. In ישעיהו, God leads a person 'on the path you go,' meaning the path he chose. In משלי, a person who chooses scoffing is pushed further into it, and a humble person is given grace.

phrases.english: From the Torah, as it is written: 'Do not go with them,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:12, where God tells בלעם not to go with בלק's messengers.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Get up, go with them.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:20. בלעם wanted to go, so now he is allowed to.

phrases.english: From the Prophets, as it is written:
'I am ה׳ your God, Who teaches you for your benefit,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:17

phrases.english: 'Who leads you on the path you go.'
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; either way it means 'the path you go.'

phrases.english: From the Writings, as it is written:
'If it is for the scoffers, He makes him scoff,'
phrases.notes: משלי 3:34

phrases.english: 'and to the humble He gives grace.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הַתּוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the three sources promised in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The statement that a person is led along the path he chooses
steps.whatToRemember: A person's own choice sets his direction, and from Above he is helped along whichever path he chooses, good or bad.

steps.title: A גואל הדם who kills the רוצח is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Back to the הלכות of גלות. רב הונא rules that if a רוצח was exiled to an עיר מקלט and the גואל הדם found him and killed him, the גואל הדם is פטור. His source is the phrase 'ולו אין משפט מות', which he reads as speaking about the גואל הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If a killer was exiled to a city of refuge, and the blood redeemer found him and killed him, the blood redeemer is exempt. רב הונא holds that 'and for him there is no sentence of death' is written about the blood redeemer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side topic and returns to the laws of the רוצח. רב הונא gives a ruling about a גואל הדם who kills the רוצח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says the גואל הדם does not get the death penalty for this killing. The גמרא explains his reason: in the פסוק 'ולו אין משפט מות', he reads the word 'him' as the גואל הדם. That reading sets up the next step, where a ברייתא reads 'him' differently.

keyTerms.meaning: City of refuge, where an accidental killer goes to live
The blood redeemer, a relative of the person who was killed
He holds, introducing the reason behind the ruling

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A killer who was exiled to a city of refuge
and the blood redeemer found him and killed him,
he is exempt.
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the גואל הדם, the one who did the killing.

phrases.english: He holds: 'And for him there is no sentence of death'
phrases.notes: דברים 19:6

phrases.english: is written about the blood redeemer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁגָּלָה לְעִיר מִקְלָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of Steps 7-8 and starts a new הלכה about גלות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גואל הדם who kills a רוצח who has gone into גלות is פטור, because 'ולו אין משפט מות' is about the גואל הדם.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the פסוק is about the killer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says 'ולו אין משפט מות' speaks about the רוצח, not the גואל הדם. It proves this from 'והוא לא שנא לו מתמול שלשום', which can only describe the killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: 'And for him there is no sentence of death': the verse is speaking about the killer. Do you say it is about the killer, or is it only about the blood redeemer? When it says, 'And he did not hate him from before,' you must say the verse is speaking about the killer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's source by quoting a ברייתא that reads the same words the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's whole proof depends on 'him' meaning the גואל הדם. The ברייתא shows that the surrounding words describe someone who 'did not hate him from before.' That fits only the accidental killer, so 'him' must be the killer. If so, רב הונא is left without a source that the גואל הדם is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say X, or is it only Y? A ברייתא formula that weighs two readings
You must say, introducing the reading that has been proven
Literally 'yesterday and the day before,' meaning from before

steps.confusionAlert: The fight is over one small word: whom does 'לו' (for him) refer to? רב הונא says the גואל הדם. The ברייתא says the רוצח. Keep track of which person each side means.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'And for him there is no sentence of death':
the verse is speaking about the killer.
Do you say it is about the killer,
or is it only about the blood redeemer?
When it says:
'And he did not hate him from before,'
phrases.notes: דברים 19:4. Not hating the victim beforehand describes the accidental killer, not the relative.

phrases.english: you must say the verse is speaking about the killer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source רב הונא relies on in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that 'ולו אין משפט מות' is about the גואל הדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא proves from the nearby words 'לא שנא לו מתמול שלשום' that the פסוק describes the accidental killer, which takes away רב הונא's source.

steps.title: רב הונא follows another ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds like a different תנא. That תנא reads 'ולו אין משפט מות' as speaking about the גואל הדם, because another phrase in the same פסוק already covers the רוצח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא holds like this תנא. A ברייתא teaches: 'And for him there is no sentence of death' is about the גואל הדם. Maybe it means the killer? No. The phrase 'he did not hate him before' already speaks about the killer. So 'for him there is no sentence of death' must be about the גואל הדם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10. It shows that רב הונא is not alone, because another ברייתא reads the פסוק just as he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that one phrase in the פסוק describes the רוצח. They argue about which phrase is free to teach about the גואל הדם. This ברייתא says 'כי לא שנא הוא לו מתמול שלשום' already covers the killer. That leaves 'ולו אין משפט מות' to teach that the גואל הדם is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא: an אמורא is shown to follow one side of a תנאים argument
How do I explain this phrase? (It must teach something else.)
The killer is already mentioned, so another phrase is free to teach something new

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ברייתות. The one in step 10 said 'ולו אין משפט מות' is about the רוצח. This one says it is about the גואל הדם. They are two different תנאים who argue.
steps.whyThisMatters: After this answer, רב הונא's ruling stands, because it has a source in a תנא.

phrases.english: He states [his view] in line with this tanna,
phrases.notes: 'He' means רב הונא, the one challenged in the last step.

phrases.english: as it is taught:
"And for him there is no sentence of death" —
the verse is speaking about the blood redeemer.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּגוֹאֵל הַדָּם הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: You say the verse is speaking about the blood redeemer,
or is it really only about the killer?
When it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי לֹא שׂוֹנֵא הוּא לוֹ מִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם״ –
phrases.english: "For he did not hate him before" —
phrases.notes: דברים 19:6, the same פסוק that says 'ולו אין משפט מות'.

phrases.english: the killer is already mentioned,
so how do I explain:
"And for him there is no sentence of death"?
The verse is speaking about the blood redeemer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the ruling depends on an argument between תנאים, and רב הונא follows one side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's reading seemed to go against the only ברייתא on the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another ברייתא reads the פסוק the way רב הונא does, so his ruling has a source.

steps.title: Challenge from the two תלמידי חכמים in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says two תלמידי חכמים travel with the רוצח to speak to the גואל הדם. Perhaps they warn him that he will be killed if he kills, which would go against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: they give the killer two Torah scholars to go with him, in case the blood redeemer tries to kill him on the way, and the scholars will speak to him. Isn't it that they warn the blood redeemer that if he kills, he will get the death penalty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new attack on רב הונא, this time from our משנה. It suggests the scholars give the גואל הדם a formal death-penalty warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A formal warning only makes sense if the גואל הדם would really be punished for killing. The משנה is about the רוצח on the road to the עיר מקלט, which is exactly רב הונא's case. If the scholars warn the גואל הדם that he will be put to death, that goes straight against רב הונא's ruling that he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that…? A way of suggesting a reading in order to challenge
They give him a formal warning, which is needed before a בית דין can punish

phrases.english: We learned [in the Mishnah]:
They give him two Torah scholars,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the רוצח on his way to the עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: in case [the blood redeemer] kills him on the way,
and they will speak to him.
Isn't it that they warn him,
that if he kills, he is liable to death?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו דְּמַתְרוּ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא challenge is answered, a new challenge comes from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a גואל הדם who kills the רוצח is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the scholars give the גואל הדם a death-penalty warning, then he can be punished for killing the רוצח.

steps.title: The scholars only speak gently
steps.stepSummary: No, the scholars do not threaten. A ברייתא explains that they speak calming words and ask the גואל הדם not to treat an accidental killer like a murderer.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. As a ברייתא teaches: 'and they will speak to him' means fitting words. They tell him: don't treat him the way murderers are treated, because the killing happened to him by accident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge. It shows that 'speaking to him' means calming him down, not warning him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on reading 'וידברו אליו' as a legal warning. The ברייתא shows it means words of persuasion asking for mercy. So the משנה says nothing about the גואל הדם being punished, and רב הונא is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Words fitting for him: calming, persuading words

phrases.english: No, as it is taught:
"And they will speak to him" —
words that are fitting for him.
They say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַל תִּנְהַג בּוֹ מִנְהַג שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים,
phrases.english: Do not treat him the way murderers are treated,
it was by accident that the act came to his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading suggested in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof against רב הונא, not the משנה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed 'speaking' means a legal warning. It really means gentle persuasion.
steps.whatToRemember: The two תלמידי חכמים calm the גואל הדם down. They don't threaten him, so the משנה does not go against רב הונא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the killer speaks for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the רוצח also speaks for himself, learning it from 'וזה דבר הרצח'. The חכמים answer that a messenger often gets more done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: he speaks for himself, as it says, 'And this is the matter of the killer.' They said to him: Much is achieved through a messenger.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with an argument about who does the talking to the גואל הדם. Is it the רוצח himself, or the scholars sent for him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'דבר' (matter) as 'speaking', so the killer himself pleads his case with the גואל הדם. The חכמים answer that much gets done through messengers, so the scholars sent with him do the speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: By himself, on his own behalf
The matter of the killer. רבי מאיר reads 'דבר' as speech

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
He speaks on his own behalf,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the רוצח himself, speaking to the גואל הדם.

phrases.english: as it says: "And this is the matter of the killer."
phrases.notes: דברים 19:4.

phrases.english: They said to him: Much is achieved through a messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הוּא מְדַבֵּר עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the רוצח pleads for himself. חכמים: messengers do it better.

steps.title: Why say it was by accident?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא looks at the ברייתא's words 'בשגגה בא מעשה לידו' and asks why they are needed. Only a שוגג goes to גלות anyway, doesn't he?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: it was by accident that the act came to his hand. Isn't that obvious? If it had been on purpose, would he be sent to exile?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the ברייתא from step 13. It asks why that phrase was needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone in an עיר מקלט seems to be a שוגג, so telling the גואל הדם 'it was an accident' seems to add nothing. The question assumes a מזיד never goes to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious! Why does this need to be said?
Someone who is sent to גלות

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: בִּשְׁגָגָה בָּא מַעֲשֶׂה לְיָדוֹ.
phrases.english: The Master said: It was by accident that the act came to his hand.
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is the ברייתא quoted in step 13.

phrases.english: That's obvious!
For if it were on purpose, would he be one who goes to exile?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: בִּשְׁגָגָה בָּא מַעֲשֶׂה לְיָדוֹ. פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at a phrase from the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the ברייתא need to say the killing was accidental?

steps.title: Yes, a מזיד can also go to גלות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers 'yes'. In some cases even a מזיד goes to גלות, so the phrase is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question with one word: yes, even a מזיד can be sent to גלות. It is setting up an explanation of when this happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a מזיד can sometimes be found in an עיר מקלט, the words 'it was by accident' are not obvious. They tell the גואל הדם that this particular killer is a שוגג.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין' here is Aramaic for 'yes'. It is not the Hebrew word אין (there is not).

phrases.english: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, even a מזיד goes to גלות in some cases, so the ברייתא's words are needed.

steps.title: At first, both the accidental and the intentional killer run to the cities of refuge
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה supports Step 16. At first, both a שוגג and a מזיד run to the ערי מקלט, and בית דין sends for them and brings them back from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: At first, both an accidental killer and an intentional killer hurry to the cities of refuge. Then בית דין sends for them and brings them back from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up what it just said in Step 16: sometimes even a מזיד goes to an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 claimed that a מזיד can also end up in גלות, so the words 'בשגגה בא מעשה לידו' are needed. This ברייתא confirms it: right after the killing, nobody knows yet who is a שוגג and who is a מזיד, so both run to the עיר מקלט. Only later does בית דין bring them back and judge them.

keyTerms.meaning: Cities of refuge, where an accidental killer is protected

steps.confusionAlert: Usually 'וְהָא תַּנְיָא' opens a challenge. Here it supports what the גמרא just said.

phrases.english: And so it is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: These words often start a challenge, but here they bring support for the last answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
At first, both the accidental killer and the intentional killer
hurry to the cities of refuge,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית דִּין שׁוֹלְחִין וּמְבִיאִין אוֹתָם מִשָּׁם.
phrases.english: and the court sends for them and brings them from there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to prove Step 16's claim that a מזיד also goes to the עיר מקלט at first.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that sometimes even a מזיד goes to an עיר מקלט
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: at first both the שוגג and the מזיד run to the ערי מקלט

steps.title: The court decides each killer's fate: death, freedom, or return to exile
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with what happens after the trial. One found liable for death is executed. One not liable is freed. One liable for גלות is sent back to the עיר מקלט. Each outcome comes from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever was found liable for death, they killed him, as it says: 'The elders of his city shall send and take him from there and hand him over to the גואל הדם, and he shall die.' Whoever was not found liable, they freed him, as it says: 'The congregation shall save the killer from the hand of the גואל הדם.' Whoever was found liable for גלות, they return him to his place, as it says: 'The congregation shall return him to his city of refuge where he fled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the three possible results of the trial. Each one has its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why both kinds of killers run to the עיר מקלט first: the trial has not happened yet. Afterward the court sorts them. A מזיד is executed. A killer who is not liable at all goes free. A real שוגג goes back to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Found liable for the death penalty
They freed him and held him not liable

phrases.english: One who was found liable for death, they executed him,
as it is stated: 'And the elders of his city shall send'
phrases.notes: דברים 19:12

phrases.english: 'and take him from there'

phrases.aramaic: וְנָתְנוּ אֹתוֹ בְּיַד גֹּאֵל הַדָּם וָמֵת״.
phrases.english: 'and hand him over to the blood-avenger, and he shall die.'
One who was not found liable, they freed him,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהִצִּילוּ הָעֵדָה אֶת הָרֹצֵחַ מִיַּד גֹּאֵל הַדָּם״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And the congregation shall save the killer from the hand of the blood-avenger.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב גָּלוּת – מַחְזִירִין אוֹתוֹ לִמְקוֹמוֹ,
phrases.english: One who was found liable for exile, they return him to his place,
phrases.notes: 'His place' means the עיר מקלט he ran to, not his hometown.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And the congregation shall return him'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.aramaic: אֶל עִיר מִקְלָטוֹ אֲשֶׁר נָס שָׁמָּה״.
phrases.english: 'to his city of refuge where he fled.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב מִיתָה – הֲרָגוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and explains what the court does after bringing the killers back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the trial, a killer liable for death is executed, one not liable is freed, and one liable for גלות is returned to the עיר מקלט.

steps.title: רבי: the intentional killers go on their own because they are mistaken
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that the מזיד runs to the עיר מקלט on his own. He wrongly thinks the cities protect everyone. In truth they protect only the שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: They go into exile on their own. They think the cities take in both the accidental and the intentional killer. They do not know that the cities take in the accidental killer but do not take in the intentional killer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds a view about why a מזיד ends up in the עיר מקלט at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah never tells a מזיד to run to an עיר מקלט. רבי says the מזיד goes there by his own choice, because he mistakenly believes it will protect him. The city really protects only a שוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: On their own, without being told to
The cities take in and protect

phrases.english: Rabbi says: They go into exile on their own.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: כִּסְבוּרִין הֵן אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג וְאֶחָד מֵזִיד – קוֹלְטוֹת,
phrases.english: They think that the cities take in both the accidental and the intentional killer,
and they do not know
that the cities take in the accidental killer, but do not take in the intentional killer.

steps.whatToRemember: Both kinds of killers may run to an עיר מקלט at first. Only the שוגג is really protected there, and בית דין sorts them out.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: מֵעַצְמָן הֵן גּוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי's view on why a מזיד runs to the עיר מקלט at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזיד goes to the עיר מקלט on his own, by mistake. The cities protect only a שוגג.

steps.title: A city full mostly of killers does not take in a killer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a city whose population is mostly רוצחים does not take in a רוצח. He learns it from the פסוק 'וְדִבֶּר בְּאׇזְנֵי זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִיא אֶת דְּבָרָיו'. The killer's words should be his own, not the same as the elders' own words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A city whose majority are killers does not take in a killer, as it says: 'And he shall speak his words in the ears of the elders of that city.' This excludes a case where their words are the same as his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about which cities can serve as an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the killer telling his story to the elders of the city. רבי אלעזר reads 'his words' as words that are new to the listeners. If most of the city, and its elders, are killers themselves, his story would be the same as theirs, so that city does not take him in.

keyTerms.meaning: Its majority, most of its people

steps.whyThisMatters: It adds a condition for an עיר מקלט: its population cannot be mostly killers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
A city whose majority are killers does not take in a killer,
as it is stated: 'And he shall speak in the ears of the elders of that city'
phrases.notes: יהושע 20:4

phrases.english: 'his words.'
But not when their words are the same as his words.
phrases.notes: He means the elders are killers too, so they would be telling the same kind of story he is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עִיר שֶׁרוּבָּהּ רוֹצְחִים – אֵינָהּ קוֹלֶטֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about which cities qualify to protect a killer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city whose population is mostly רוצחים does not take in a רוצח. This is learned from 'אֶת דְּבָרָיו' in יהושע 20:4.

steps.title: A city with no elders does not take in a killer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that an עיר מקלט with no זקנים cannot protect a רוצח, because the פסוק requires 'the elders of the city.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר says: A city that has no elders does not take in a killer. We need 'the elders of the city,' and there are none.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second ruling about which cities can work as an עיר מקלט. A city with no זקנים cannot protect a killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the killer speaks 'in the ears of the elders of the city.' רבי אלעזר reads this as a requirement. If the city has no elders, this step cannot happen, so the city does not protect him.

keyTerms.meaning: Elders, the city's leaders and judges

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
A city that has no elders
does not take in [a killer],
since we need 'the elders of the city,' and there are none.
phrases.notes: יהושע 20:4. This is the same פסוק רבי אלעזר used in the step before.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ זְקֵנִים אֵינָהּ קוֹלֶטֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבי אלעזר, built on the same פסוק about the elders of the city as Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עיר מקלט with no זקנים does not protect a רוצח, because the פסוק requires the elders of the city.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree about a refuge city with no elders
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree whether a city with no זקנים takes in a רוצח. One says the elders are required. The other says they are only the ideal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: About a city that has no elders, רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree. One says it takes in a killer, and one says it does not. The one who says it does not holds that we need 'the elders of the city,' and there are none. The one who says it does holds that the elders are only the proper way to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the case of רבי אלעזר's ruling is disputed by רבי אמי and רבי אסי: one holds like him and one disagrees. It then explains the reason behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the פסוק mentions elders. They argue about what that means. One side says no elders means no protection. The other says speaking before elders is the ideal way, but the city still protects without them.

keyTerms.meaning: One says (we are not told which sage holds which view)
According to the one who says
Merely a מצוה: the ideal way, but not a must for the law to work

steps.confusionAlert: מצוה בעלמא does not mean the elders are pointless. It means you should do it this way, but if there are no elders, the city still works.

phrases.english: It was stated: A city that has no elders,
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi [disagree]:
one says: it takes in [a killer],
and one says: it does not take in [a killer].
According to the one who says it does not take in,
we need 'the elders of the city,' and there are none.
According to the one who says it takes in,
it is merely a מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means speaking before the elders is the right way to do it, but without them the city still protects.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: עִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ זְקֵנִים, רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אלעזר's ruling is one side of a disagreement, and gives both reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreement: either the elders are required and the city does not protect without them, or they are only the ideal way and the city still protects.

steps.title: Same disagreement about a בן סורר ומורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree whether a בן סורר ומורה can be judged in a city with no זקנים. The פסוק says his parents bring him 'to the elders of his city.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a city that has no elders, רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree. One says a boy can become a בן סורר ומורה there, and one says he cannot. The one who says he cannot holds that we need 'the elders of his city,' and there are none. The one who says he can holds that the elders are only the proper way to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case with the same disagreement. This time it is about a בן סורר ומורה in a city with no elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure is the same as the עיר מקלט case. The פסוק mentions elders, and the question is whether they are a must or just the ideal. The same two positions come back.

keyTerms.meaning: The wayward and rebellious son of דברים 21

phrases.english: And a city that has no elders:
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi [disagree]:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: נַעֲשֶׂה בָּהּ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה,
phrases.english: one says: one can become a wayward and rebellious son in it,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵין נַעֲשֶׂה בָּהּ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה.
phrases.english: and one says: one cannot become a wayward and rebellious son in it.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין נַעֲשֶׂה בָּהּ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה –
phrases.english: According to the one who says one cannot become a wayward and rebellious son in it,
we need 'the elders of his city,' and there are none.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:19

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נַעֲשֶׂה בָּהּ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה –
phrases.english: According to the one who says one can become a wayward and rebellious son in it,
it is merely a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ זְקֵנִים – רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי, חַד אָמַר: נַעֲשֶׂה בָּהּ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same disagreement and the same reasoning from Step 22 to בן סורר ומורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreement: either a בן סורר ומורה cannot be judged without elders, or the elders are only the ideal way.

steps.title: Same disagreement about an עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree whether a city with no זקנים brings an עגלה ערופה. The פסוק says 'the elders of that city' bring the calf down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a city that has no elders, רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree. One says it brings an עגלה ערופה, and one says it does not. The one who says it does not holds that we need 'the elders of that city,' and there are none. The one who says it does holds that the elders are only the proper way to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case with the same disagreement. This time it is about bringing an עגלה ערופה when the city has no elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the פסוק names the elders. One side says that without them the מצוה cannot be done at all. The other says the elders are the ideal, but the city still brings the calf.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a dead body is found and the killer is unknown

steps.whatToRemember: All three cases follow one pattern. When a פסוק mentions 'elders,' one sage says they are a must, so with no elders the law does not apply. The other says they are only the ideal way (מצוה בעלמא), so the law still applies.

phrases.english: And a city that has no elders:
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi [disagree]:
one says: it brings a heifer whose neck is broken,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה.
phrases.english: and one says: it does not bring a heifer whose neck is broken.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה –
phrases.english: According to the one who says it does not bring a heifer whose neck is broken,
we need 'the elders of that city,' and there are none.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4

phrases.english: According to the one who says it brings a heifer whose neck is broken,
it is merely a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ זְקֵנִים, רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי – חַד אָמַר: מְבִיאָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last case of the same disagreement, which closes this group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreement: either a city with no elders cannot bring an עגלה ערופה, or the elders are only the ideal way and it still brings one.

steps.title: Why was the section about killers said?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא opens a new topic by asking why the פרשה of רוצחים was said. His answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא says: For what reason was the section about killers said
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. רבי חמא בר חנינא asks why the תורה included the פרשה of רוצחים, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only sets up a question. The answer, and what is unusual about this פרשה, will come right after.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about killers and the ערי מקלט

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina says:
For what reason was the section about killers stated
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶאֶמְרָה פָּרָשַׁת רוֹצְחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the elders discussion and opens a new statement about the פרשה of רוצחים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תורה stated the פרשה of רוצחים (the question is completed and answered on the next amud).
